title: KV fragmentation and page-pool reuse strategies for paged attention
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Our paged attention implementation allocates fixed-size KV pages per request group which leads to fragmentation and low page reuse for workloads with mixed sequence lengths. This increases GPU memory pressure and causes unexpected eviction spikes during prefill bursts and long-running chat sessions. Goal: introduce a fragmentation-aware page pool and reuse policy to reduce memory waste, lower eviction frequency during prefill, and improve tail latency during decode bursts without increasing median latency.
comments: 2025-02-13 - Initial design spike complete. Measured fragmentation with synthetic mix-of-lengths benchmark; observed 18% wasted page capacity and 23% higher eviction rate on p99 under mixed workload.
2025-02-19 - Design review with runtime and infra teams. Agreed on a slab-like page pool with per-model buckets and a lightweight free-list that tracks holes by size class.

2025-02-25 - Prototype implemented: opportunistic coalescing on free, generational stamps to avoid ABA on reuse. Prototype landed in branch feature/kv-pool-reuse. GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4523
2025-03-01 - Load testing: reduced eviction events by 41% and out-of-memory incidents by 67% for our 'mixed-chat' scenario, small increase (0.6ms) in median prefill scheduling overhead.

2025-03-04 - Raised follow-ups: (1) integrate per-tenant quotas into pool; (2) expose hole metrics in Console; (3) tune generational TTL for rapid reuse workloads. Assigned follow-ups to Marco and ops.
acceptance_criteria: Reduction in average page fragmentation (measured as percent unused slots per allocated page) of at least 30% on mixed-length benchmarks compared to baseline
Eviction event rate during prefill bursts reduced by at least 30% in our synthetic workload cluster
No regression >2% in median decode latency across standard throughput profiles
Metrics surfaced in Console: page_holes, avg_hole_size, reuse_rate, generational_misses
Unit tests and stress tests added and running in CI; PR reviewed and merged
implementation_notes: Introduce PagePool component with size-classes: 64-token, 256-token, 1024-token slots to keep allocation and fragmentation bookkeeping cheap
Use stamped handles (generation counter + index) to detect stale references and avoid ABA races across concurrent decode/prefill paths
On free: try fast coalesce with adjacent free pages in same size class; if coalesce cross-size needed, move to deferred coalesce to avoid long critical sections
Per-model and per-tenant pools: keep lightweight accounting to avoid noisy neighbors, but default to global pool when tenant not specified
Prefill scheduler should consult pool reuse score to decide whether to reuse existing hole or allocate new page; add backpressure if pool exhaustion predicted
Eviction policy: prefer reclaiming low-reuse generation pages first; mark pages with low reuse as candidates for compaction during low-load windows
Expose prometheus metrics for fragmentation and reuse and a Console dashboard for per-model heatmaps
Integrate with existing KV compaction job (ENG-7832) to run periodic consolidation during off-peak hours
test_plan: Unit: allocator correctness, stamped-handle ABA tests, free/coalesce semantics
Integration: end-to-end paged attention with mixed-length model traces; assert no memory leaks after 1M requests in simulation
Load: cluster-level replay using 'mixed-chat' scenario (50% short, 30% medium, 20% long sequences) at 75% capacity for 4h to validate eviction reduction
Regression: decode latency/throughput A/B tests against canary baseline using same traffic shape
Chaos: simulate sudden spike in prefill rate and ensure pool backpressure prevents OOMs and keeps p99 within SLO
rollout_plan: Canary rollout to runtime-north-1 (5%) with aggressive observability enabled
Monitor reuse_rate and eviction events for 24h, rollback if eviction increases or p99 latency regresses >15%
Gradual ramp to 25% then 75% over 72h with targeted tenants enabled if metrics pass
Full global rollout in runtime-1.20 if no regressions and Console dashboard validated
Follow-up ticket to enable per-tenant tuning and KMS-protected metrics export
benchmark_summary: Baseline (runtime-1.18 mixed-chat): avg_fragmentation=18%, eviction_rate=9.2 evictions/min, p99_decode_latency=152ms. Prototype with pool: avg_fragmentation=10.5% (-41%), eviction_rate=5.4 evictions/min (-41%), p99_decode_latency=145ms (-4.6%), median prefill overhead +0.6ms. Memory headroom improved by ~12% in 8-GPU pod tests.
notes: Trade-offs: slab-like pools reduce fragmentation but add a slight allocation path cost. We mitigate with small size-classes and fast-path reuse. Need to watch multi-tenant fairness; initial approach favors per-model buckets with soft quotas. Follow-ups will add strict quota enforcement if noisy neighbor issues are observed. Also evaluate combining this with compressed KV pages in Optimize later.
